specification.problem: Continuous-time quantum walk spatial search for a marked site w on a small periodic honeycomb (graphene) lattice, using the Dirac point at E=0, with a tunable marking onsite energy; plus a two-site marked state-transfer variant. Output is the probability of the bitstring of w read from position-register counts.
specification.reconstruction_scope: One smallest instance: periodic honeycomb of 2x2 unit cells (8 sites, 3 position qubits, no padding), Hamiltonian H=-gamma A - epsilon|w><w|, first-order Trotterized evolution, uniform-superposition initial state, gamma and epsilon scanned numerically, and measurement of all 3 qubits. Outside scope: analytic scaling in N, the paper's specific marking variants and exact parameters, the Dirac-eigenstate preparation circuit for larger lattices, larger lattices, and a full transfer study.

symbols.meaning: adjacency matrix of the periodic honeycomb lattice (bipartite)
symbols.domain: N x N real symmetric 0/1 matrix, N=8

symbols.meaning: marking onsite energy strength (tunable, not necessarily gamma)
marked site index; site i corresponds to bit i of the position register (little-endian)

equations.label: Search Hamiltonian
equations.description: Lattice hopping plus onsite marking potential on the target site
equations.abstract_quote: making a change to standard methods of marking a particular site in the lattice
equations.justification: The abstract implies a CTQW on a graphene lattice with a modified marking; the specific form is the standard Hamiltonian with a tunable epsilon (assumption).
assumptions: epsilon is tuned, not fixed to gamma

equations.label: Dirac point of the bipartite lattice
equations.description: The Dirac point lies at zero energy of the unmarked graphene spectrum; the resonance scan targets coupling of this state to the marked site
equations.abstract_quote: utilising the Dirac point in the energy spectrum
equations.justification: The abstract says the Dirac point is used; E=0 is standard for the honeycomb tight-binding model.
assumptions: On a tiny periodic lattice the zero-energy states may be few or degenerate and should be checked numerically

equations.label: Trotterized evolution
equations.description: First-order product formula with the three perfect matchings of the honeycomb as commuting edge-colour layers; the oracle phase is a multi-controlled phase gate. Layers should be ordered consistently.
equations.justification: A standard Trotter decomposition proposed for circuit implementation; step size and order are not from the abstract.
assumptions: Delta t small enough for fidelity
Edge colouring into 3 matchings exists (the 2x2 periodic case may have multi-edges, so the lattice must be checked)
Each edge term is a two-qubit gate in permutation-conjugated form

equations.label: Initial state and success probability
equations.description: Uniform superposition start by Hadamards; readout is the counts frequency of the bitstring of w
equations.justification: Sketch choice; the Dirac eigenstate start is an alternative.
assumptions: Counts bitstring key read as bits[::-1] gives the site index

equations.label: Two-site transfer
equations.latex: |\psi_0\rangle=|s\rangle,\quad H_T=-\gamma A-\epsilon(|s\rangle\langle s|+|r\rangle\langle r|),\quad t^*\approx\frac{\pi}{2J_{\rm eff}}
equations.description: Amplitude transfer between s and r with equal onsite energies; J_eff is the effective coupling splitting between the two resonant eigenstates, determined numerically
equations.abstract_quote: transfer probability amplitude across the lattice between specific lattice sites
equations.justification: The abstract claims transfer between sites; the Hamiltonian and t* form follow the sketch and are assumed, not stated.
assumptions: J_eff computed numerically from the spectrum

registers.name: pos
registers.role: site index, little-endian, measured at the end

specification.initial_state: Hadamard on all position qubits (uniform superposition) for search; basis state |s> for transfer

steps.description: Classically build A for the 2x2 periodic honeycomb, verify the bipartite structure and Dirac-point zero modes, and choose the edge colouring and site-to-bit map.
Prepare the initial state with H gates.
Apply r Trotter steps of the three matching layers plus the marking phase (a multi-controlled phase with X conjugation on the zero bits of w). Each oracle placement is one query.
Scan gamma, epsilon and r classically (statevector or numeric) to pick the resonance and the peak time; for transfer use eq_5.
Measure all position qubits and read the frequency of the bitstring of w, reversing the key to map bits to sites.

specification.measurement: Measure all position qubits into classical bits with measure(i,i); site index i is bit i, read with bits[::-1].
specification.classical_postprocessing: Estimate P_w as the count fraction of w's bitstring; choose the gamma, epsilon and t with the maximum value.
assumptions: 8-site periodic honeycomb, all qubits within the cap
Marking strength epsilon differs from gamma and is tuned numerically
Optimal parameters are found numerically, not analytically
